name: X API pay-per-usage (official)
what: Official X developer pricing page: pay-per-usage with no subscription tiers; per-unit charges for post reads and creates.
why_it_matters: The only fully legal route to a person's X posts with official IDs, timestamps and referenced_tweets (retweet/quote metadata). Cheapest legal option found for most people; the falsifier target (X API Pro at $5,000/mo) is no longer the comparator.
numbers: Post read $0.005/resource; post create $0.015/request; Owned Reads $0.001/resource; read cap 3,000,000 post reads per monthly billing cycle; Enterprise not priced publicly (page says upgrade via interest form). Source: docs.x.com pricing page as fetched 2026-10-14 (no date shown on page). Vendor blogs (postproxy.dev, zernio.com) conflict on read price ($0.005 vs $0.01 vs $0.015 create) and on Basic ($200/mo) and Pro ($5,000/mo) being legacy-only, with one blog saying Basic was force-migrated 1 June 2026 (unverified).
ui_notes: Show cost as reads x $0.005 with a monthly cap counter; surface 3M/mo cap as a hard stop for big accounts; keep per-person read ledger to avoid re-reading.
note: ToS: official, licensed use; X developer agreement (June 2025) bars using X content or API to train or fine-tune foundation or frontier models, so do not feed posts into model training. Maintenance: official, high. Price sources disagree; re-check the live console before budgeting. | check: docs.x.com pricing (2026-10-14): post read $0.005/resource, post create $0.015/request, owned reads $0.001/resource, pay-per-usage cap 3M post reads per billing cycle; Enterprise not priced.

name: yt-dlp
what: Command-line downloader and metadata extractor for YouTube (channel video lists with dates, auto-caption subtitles, audio download).
